source.edition: Elementary Topology, Michael C. Gemignani, Second Edition
source.visualReview: Full supplied PDF pages 55, 101, 102, 106, 107 and 108 inspected with adjacent mathematical prose; all five final native SVG renderings inspected beside source crops.
source.boundsConvention: sourceBounds is normalized [x,y,width,height] against the full PDF page. Inspected pixel crops include graphic and labels, excluding captions and prose.

implementation.semantics: Immutable shape-free Substance snapshots describe relative topology, clopen lower-limit products, exact dyadic neighborhood relations and continuous map extensions.
implementation.styleReuse: lowerLimitProductStyle renders basic neighborhoods and affine subspace intersections; dyadicNeighborhoodStyle renders separation and induction excerpts. All three policies share topologyDrawing, native vector hatching, labels and subdued orange palette.
implementation.graphics: Native Penrose PathData, lines, equations and clipped hatch groups. No bitmap or raw SVG image wrappers.
implementation.interactive: Every build factory accepts final optional FigureRenderOptions with variation/interactive forwarded to assembly; canonical default seeds and source geometry remain fixed.

verification.domainRuntimeImport: passed after all declarations were exported
verification.formatting: Prettier applied to new source/test files
verification.visualReview: Five optimized SVGs rendered and rasterized on white backgrounds, compared side by side with inspected source crops. Figure 5.12 label sizes were corrected after comparison. Root review removed an extra A outline from Figure 5.12 and reduced its label knockout to match the source.
verification.scope: Boundary membership, relative topology witnesses, dyadic inclusion chains, exact path boundary agreement, positive sampled Jacobian of the illustrative patch and native SVG structure are checked; formal universal proofs and pixel identity are not claimed.

figures.sourceContext: Example 14 (continued from supplied printed page 103): the product of the lower-limit topology from Chapter 3 Example 11 has clopen basic rectangles [x,a) times [y,b). Each rectangle equals its closure; the plane is regular, although it is not normal.
geometry: A hatched rectangle above and left of the origin, with solid included left/bottom edges and the source round half-open marks at the opposite corners.
Original x, y, (0,0) and southwest (x,y) labels are retained; only the southwest corner is marked.
facts: LowerLimitTopology on the real line; Regular, Normal and T1 for the factor, ProductTopologyOf for the plane, and Regular/T1/T3/NotNormal for the product.
Two factual half-open interval descriptors, their clopen product neighborhood, its southwest point, and ClosureOf(U,U,tau).
Pixel positions and hatch geometry are confined to Style.
checks: Membership includes the southwest corner and left/bottom edges; strict top/right boundaries are excluded.
Native SVG retains both half-open hooks, one point marker, clipped vector hatching and no image elements.
limits: The finite diagram illustrates a typical neighborhood, rather than proving the universal separation properties.
Upper/right hatch limits represent excluded boundaries; no solid top/right outline is introduced.

figures.sourceContext: The same example takes Y={(x,y):x+y=0}. A northeast basic neighborhood at a point of Y meets Y only at that point, so the induced subspace topology is discrete; Y is closed in the product plane. The following nonnormality discussion in the book explicitly omits a rigorous proof.
geometry: The downward antidiagonal Y passes through the origin and the included southwest rectangle corner.
Same clopen rectangle policy as 5.9, with the source Y label and no extra point dot or corner label.
facts: AffineSubspace Y has coefficients [1,1,0], ClosedIn(Y,tau), and a Discrete induced topology.
IntersectionOf(singleton,U,Y), SingletonOf(singleton,anchor) and Member(anchor,Y) encode the mathematical singleton intersection.
checks: 201 sampled antidiagonal points meet the half-open rectangle only when the displacement from its southwest corner is zero.
The singleton identity, induced discrete topology and native vector antidiagonal are checked.
limits: The pictured singleton explains discreteness, not the subsequent universal nonnormality argument.
Nonnormality is a named mathematical property of the specified lower-limit product, not inferred from finite drawing overlap.

figures.sourceContext: Urysohn lemma construction in a T4 space: disjoint nonempty closed A,B and dyadic indexed open sets satisfy A subset U(q), B disjoint U(q), and Cl U(q) subset U(q prime) for q<q prime.
geometry: Separate small B at lower left; small A lies inside the U(q)/Cl U(q) contour and the outer U(q prime) contour.
The original unfilled outlines and A, B, U(q), Cl U(q), U(q prime) labels are retained; no hatching is added to this source outline figure.
facts: DyadicOpenFamily with generic closed A,B and T4 topology; default exact dyadic witnesses q=1/4 and q prime=3/4.
DyadicIndexOf, SetInFamily, OpenIn, Subset(A,U), Disjoint(B,U), ClosureOf and the next-neighborhood inclusion.
checks: Both relative closedness facts, disjointness and T4 requirement are checked before drawing.
Actual SVG has four unfilled native outlines and no hatch masks.
limits: The two shown neighborhoods form a finite excerpt of the infinite dyadic construction.
U(q) and its closure share the visible source outline; their mathematical entities and closure fact remain distinct.

figures.sourceContext: Inductive insertion of U(n/2^(k+1)) between the already defined neighboring dyadic neighborhoods for odd n. The prose explicitly gives Cl U((n-1)/2^(k+1)) subset U(n/2^(k+1)) subset Cl U(n/2^(k+1)) subset U((n+1)/2^(k+1)).
geometry: Three irregular nested hatch regions, source diagonal/vertical/cross hatch distinctions, and a small central A label on a white knockout. No added A outline is drawn.
Three original fractional U labels and leader lines. Fraction label size was adjusted after actual rendering to keep all labels within the source framing.
facts: Default n=3,k=2 produces exact indices 1/4,3/8,1/2; alternate valid odd numerator/exponent values are supported by the shape-free factory.
DyadicRefinementStep retains both closures and the complete ordered inclusion chain.
checks: Bounded exact binary index helpers reject invalid, even or unrepresentable refinement indices.
The mathematical middle index is 3/8 with the correct k+1 exponent.
The actual SVG source label override, three clipping groups, small central A label without an additional boundary loop and native hatch lines are checked.
figures.sourceDiscrepancy: The source graphic literally labels the middle region U(n/2^k), while its adjacent induction prose requires U(n/2^(k+1)). The book build preserves the visible source label through a Style-only override. The reusable default style and all Substance indices follow the mathematically ordered k+1 construction.
limits: Hatch density is lighter than the scan and uses the consistent pale orange palette; the three source hatch modes remain distinguishable.
The finite displayed step is not a formal proof of the infinite Urysohn family.

figures.sourceContext: Example 17: A is the union of the two horizontal closed edges in I times I. A continuous f:A to R squared has a continuous extension F across the normal square. Thus any two paths in R squared are freely homotopic; no endpoint-fixing condition is stated.
geometry: A hatched unit square labeled by the original top/bottom edge set notation, an unlabelled arrow, and a warped hatched image patch beside coordinate axes.
Top/bottom paths are sampled as native curves; the two connecting sides and interior deformation form a continuous illustrative extension.
facts: ClosedProductRectangle with bounds [0,0,1,1], HorizontalBoundaryPair A, a finite two-edge family and UnionOf(A,family).
Two continuous TopologicalPath objects, their boundary map f, ExtensionOf(F,f,A,square), relative ClosedIn and induced SubspaceTopologyOf, and both continuous map facts.
No drawing samples or pixel positions are stored in Substance.
checks: Every lower and upper boundary sample agrees exactly with its named path, even with interior deformation.
361 interior samples have positive numerical Jacobian for the displayed illustrative patch.
Substance contains only the two horizontal edges in A, not the full square boundary.
Actual SVG contains separate clipped square/image regions, a 128-point native image contour and no raster wrappers.
limits: The book supplies generic curves without analytic formulas. The cubic path samplers and continuous t(1-t) interior deformation are Style realizations, not formulas attributed to the source.
Caller samplers can represent other continuous paths; finite sampled contours are schematic, and filling arbitrary folded map images is not claimed.
There are no imposed equal endpoints or fixed-endpoint homotopy claims.
